_about: Realistic student questions for the answering layer (written 2026-11-09). 'no_video' questions are asked with no tutorial loaded; 'video_context' questions are asked after loading the saved step list named in `video` (fixtures steps_<id>.json: real extractions of the video, prompt v9). behaviours: answer = a real answer is expected; answer_or_admit = a correct answer or an honest 'I do not know / not covered' is acceptable, a wrong or invented one is not; clarify_or_admit = a question back or an honest 'not covered'; admit = the sources cannot contain the answer, so an honest 'not available' is the right outcome and any specific claim is wrong. must_any = every inner list needs at least one of its words (case-insensitive) in an ANSWERED reply; must_not = words that must not appear. reference is what a correct answer says, written from the application documentation as the author knows it; it is not produced by the system under test. Automated checks sort replies; a person reads every answered reply for correctness (see the evaluation report).

questions.question: how do i extrude a bone in blender
questions.reference: Select the armature, enter Edit Mode (Tab), select a bone or its tip, press E and move the mouse to extrude a new connected bone.

questions.question: wat is the diffrence between object mode and edit mode
questions.reference: Object Mode works on whole objects (move, rotate, scale, join); Edit Mode changes the object's own geometry (vertices, edges, faces) or, for an armature, its bones.

questions.question: how do i add ik to a leg bone
questions.reference: Enter Pose Mode, select the lower (shin) bone, open the Bone Constraints tab, Add Bone Constraint > Inverse Kinematics, and set Chain Length (2 reaches the thigh); optionally add a target and a pole target.

questions.question: my knee wont bend when i use ik
questions.reference: Common causes: chain length not set to 2 (the IK reaches the root), bones perfectly straight so the solver has no bend direction (give the knee a slight pre-bend), or a pole target/angle that is off.

questions.question: i parented mesh to armature with automatic weights but the mesh dont move
questions.reference: Select the mesh, then the armature (armature active), Ctrl+P > With Automatic Weights. If the mesh does not follow: check the Armature modifier exists, you are posing in Pose Mode, bones have Deform enabled, and scale is applied; automatic weights can fail on bad geometry.

questions.question: i pressed tab on my armature and nothing happens
questions.reference: Tab toggles Edit Mode for the active object and only works with the mouse over the 3D viewport; the armature must be the active selected object. (In Pose Mode Tab behaves differently; Ctrl+Tab switches Pose Mode.)

questions.question: how do i join 2 objects
questions.reference: In Object Mode select both objects (the one you select last stays active), press Ctrl+J or Object > Join.

questions.question: which mode do i use to paint weights
questions.reference: Weight Paint Mode (mode dropdown in the 3D viewport header), with the mesh active.

questions.question: whats the best render engine to use
questions.reference: It depends on the goal (Cycles for path-traced quality, EEVEE for speed); a good answer asks what for or says it depends, and never names one as simply best.

questions.question: how to make left and right side of the skeleton the same
questions.reference: In Edit Mode on the armature select the bones, Armature > Symmetrize (bones named with .L/.R suffixes are mirrored across the X axis); or use X-Axis Mirror while editing.

questions.question: how do i make an ik handel in maya
questions.reference: Rigging menu set > Skeleton > Create IK Handle (IK Handle Tool): click the start joint, then the end joint of the chain; an IK handle appears at the end joint.

questions.question: maya knee flips when i move the ik handle
questions.reference: A flipping knee usually means the rotate-plane IK has no stable bend direction: set a preferred angle on the chain before creating the handle, and/or use a pole vector constraint, keeping the pole control off the leg's straight line.

questions.question: what does freeze transformations do
questions.reference: Modify > Freeze Transformations sets the current translate, rotate and scale values to their defaults (0, 0, 0 and 1) without moving the object, so a control starts clean; it is used before building rigs.

questions.question: how do i bind skin to the joints
questions.reference: Select the root joint and the mesh (or the joints and mesh), then Rigging menu set > Skin > Bind Skin > Smooth Bind (default options).

questions.question: skin weights look bad around the elbow how do i fix
questions.reference: Use the Paint Skin Weights Tool on the mesh: select the elbow joint, paint or smooth influence in the crease, keep Normalize Weights on, then optionally prune small weights.

questions.question: how to orient joints so x points down the bone
questions.reference: Select the joints, Skeleton > Orient Joint (options): Primary Axis X, a Secondary Axis (Y or Z) and a Secondary Axis World Orientation so the bend plane is consistent.

questions.question: difference between ik and fk
questions.reference: FK: you rotate each joint down the chain, the child follows the parent. IK: you place the end of the chain (the handle) and a solver computes the joint rotations.

questions.question: what key is the rotate tool in maya
questions.reference: E (W is Move, R is Scale, Q is Select).

questions.question: after mirror joint my chain is facing the wrong way
questions.reference: In Skeleton > Mirror Joint options choose the mirror plane (for example YZ) and the Mirroring Behavior (Behavior keeps mirrored axes, Orientation keeps the original orientation); the wrong option flips the joint axes.

questions.question: can i do cloth simulation in maya with ncloth
questions.reference: Yes, nCloth (Nucleus) is Maya's cloth simulation. The project's knowledge base covers rigging, so an honest 'not covered here' is acceptable; inventing a procedure is not.

questions.question: how do i make a skeleton in houdini
questions.reference: In a Geometry network add a Skeleton SOP (KineFX); with the node selected press Enter in the viewport to draw joints by clicking, and finish with Enter/Esc.

questions.question: what does the rig doctor node do
questions.reference: Rig Doctor inspects a KineFX skeleton or rig for problems and can fix them (for example bad joint hierarchy or transforms) before deformation.

questions.question: how to bind a mesh to the skeleton in houdini
questions.reference: Compute capture weights with a capture node (for example Joint Capture Biharmonic or Bone Capture Proximity) taking the mesh and skeleton, then deform with Joint Deform (or Bone Deform).

questions.question: houdni kinefx mirror skeleton
questions.reference: Use the Skeleton Mirror SOP on the skeleton, choosing the mirror plane and the naming for the new side.

questions.question: all my joints are at the origin
questions.reference: Too vague to answer well: a good reply asks what node/step this is after (drawing the skeleton, importing, capturing) or states it cannot tell.

questions.question: difference between kinefx and apex
questions.reference: KineFX is Houdini's SOP-based rigging and animation framework (skeletons as geometry); APEX is the newer graph-based rig and animation system in Houdini 20 and later that builds on KineFX ideas.

questions.question: which node makes ik chains
questions.reference: The IK Chains SOP (KineFX) solves IK on chains defined by start and end joints.

questions.question: how do i show the joint names in the viewport
questions.reference: KineFX tutorials use a Marker or display option to show joint names; the exact setting depends on the version. An honest 'not sure' is acceptable; an invented menu path is not.

questions.question: what is a wrangle
questions.reference: An Attribute Wrangle is a node that runs a short VEX snippet over points, primitives or other elements. Outside the rigging scope: an honest 'not covered' is acceptable.

questions.question: how do i animate a walk cycle in houdini
questions.reference: Broad: a good reply asks which approach (keyframing a rig, APEX, KineFX motion clips) or says it is outside what it covers.
